description.summary: an allow/deny prompt for privileged requests

protocol.description:
Lets a privileged, compositor-trusted client (in practice, this compositor's own xdg-desktop-portal backends) ask that an "app X wants to do Y" prompt be shown to the user, and report back their answer.
This is deliberately not exposed to ordinary clients: the manager global is only advertised to clients connected through the compositor's privileged capture socket (see `crate::screencopy`), the same channel used for `ext-image-capture-source-v1`/`ext-image-copy-capture-v1`. A prompt only ever names an `app_id` and a human-readable reason chosen by the trusted caller, never anything the prompted-about app itself can influence directly.
Two privileged roles use this same manager global: a *requester* (an xdg-desktop-portal backend) calls `prompt` to ask for one; a *renderer* (in practice, this compositor's companion shell) calls `set_renderer` once to take over showing every prompt as `show`/`cancel` events and answering them via `answer`. If no renderer has registered - the shell isn't running yet, or isn't built with support for this protocol - the compositor falls back to drawing a minimal prompt of its own and reading Enter/Escape directly, so a prompt is never simply lost.

interface.name: ironland_permission_prompt_manager_v1
interface.description: This interface allows a privileged client to ask that a permission prompt be shown (as a requester), or to take over showing every prompt itself (as a renderer).

request.name: prompt
request.description: Queues a prompt for display. If another prompt is already showing, this one waits its turn. Exactly one of `allowed`/`denied` is sent to the returned object once the user answers.

arg.name: app_id
arg.summary: requesting application id, shown to the user

arg.name: reason
arg.summary: human-readable description of what's being requested

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying the manager doesn't affect prompts already created through it, nor does it un-register this client as the renderer if it was one (there is currently no way to do that short of disconnecting).

request.name: set_renderer
request.description: Registers this client as the prompt renderer: from now on, every prompt (including any already queued when this is called) is described to it via `show` instead of being drawn by the compositor itself, and only this client's `answer` requests resolve them. Only one renderer is tracked at a time; a second caller replaces the first (e.g. the shell restarting).

event.name: show
event.description: Sent only to the registered renderer, once per prompt, in the order prompts were requested. `prompt_id` is opaque and unrelated to any `ironland_permission_prompt_v1` object id (renderer and requester are different clients, so object ids between them don't correspond) - pass it back to `answer`.

event.name: cancel

description.summary: a shown-but-unanswered prompt is no longer relevant

event.description: Sent only to the registered renderer, if a prompt named by a prior `show` is destroyed by its requester (e.g. it disconnected or timed out) before `answer` was called for it. The renderer should stop showing it, if it still is.

request.name: answer
request.description: Resolves the prompt named `prompt_id` (from a prior `show` event on this same connection). Ignored (a protocol no-op, not an error - the prompt may have just been cancelled) if `prompt_id` doesn't name a currently-pending prompt, or if this client isn't the registered renderer.

description.summary: a queued or showing permission prompt

event.name: allowed
event.description: Sent at most once, when the user (or the registered renderer, on their behalf) answers yes.

event.name: denied

description.summary: the user denied the request, or the prompt was cancelled

event.description: Sent at most once, when the user (or the registered renderer) answers no, or when the prompt is destroyed by the compositor before being answered (e.g. session teardown).

request.name: destroy
request.description: If not yet answered, this cancels it (dismissing it from the queue, or from the screen if it was showing, and sending `cancel` to the registered renderer if there is one) with no `allowed`/`denied` event sent for it.
